newsitem.title: USA: LOOP evacuates offshore U.S. Gulf platform.
newsitem.headline: LOOP evacuates offshore U.S. Gulf platform.

text.p: The Louisiana Offshore Oil Port continued to operate onshore facilities and evacuated a platform in the Gulf of Mexico which lies in the forecast track of Tropical Storm Danny, officials said.
No cargoes were due in today and crews will assess whether a single cargo due in on Friday would be delayed, officials said.
"(Danny) has not directly affected any operations yet. We've taken non-essentials off the platform," a dispatcher on the platform about 20 miles south of Grand Isle, La. said.

The National Hurricane Center at noon EDT said the storm's center reformed to the northeast to latitude 28.6 north, longitude 90.9 west or about 115 miles southwest of New Orleans moving northeast at about 5 miles an hour.
Danny was on track to make landfall late Thursday or early Friday, and a tropical storm warning and hurricane watch were raised from Cameron, La., to Orange Beach in east Alabama.
Houston-based Wilkens Weather Technologies was predicting landfall south of Port Fourchon, La., on the east side of Timbalier Bay, about 25 miles southwest of Houma.
